observed_original_abi.calling_convention: none asserted. The body is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall: it names no memory operand relative to ESP or to any register, so it has 0 ordinary stack arguments, and its bare RET pops nothing. The derived ABI record lists all four as candidates and abstains for want of a discriminator ('no_discriminator: no stack-argument read and no positive receiver evidence'). The reconstruction therefore declares the entry with no convention macro at all and types the slot as a plain namespace-scope object, which is what an absolute-address accessor is.
observed_original_abi.receiver: none. Opcode 0xa1 takes a 32-bit absolute address as its only operand and has NO ModRM byte and NO base register, so there is no receiver to name. The derived record agrees: receiver.present false, distinct_offsets 0, register null, bounds_only true.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the 32-bit word STORED at the absolute address 0x0169e294, copied bit for bit into EAX and re-typed as a pointer; no arithmetic, no masking, no sign extension, no comparison and no branch.
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: MODELLED AS A POINTER ON WRITER AND CALLER EVIDENCE, NOT ON THE DERIVED RECORD'S CLASS. The derived ABI record's register_class pointer_like is INFERRED with corroboration not_available and cannot distinguish a loaded word from a computed address, so it is not the reason for this type. Two independent facts are. (1) The only recorded writer of the slot, the function at 0x00d3b9b0, is a constructor-shaped body that stores its own incoming object pointer into the slot at 0x00d3baae (MOV [0x0169e294], ESI) and then returns that same pointer, so the slot is published as an object address. (2) Callers use the result as an address: the caller at 0x00d4c5e0 calls this entry twice and each time moves the result into ECX before calling a member function (0x00d39360, live signature 'App__cCreatureModeStrategy__ExecuteAction(cCreatureModeStrategy *this, ...)'), and readers at 0x00d395a4, 0x00d2b6e0 and 0x00d2c280 index through the loaded word at displacements 0x24, 0xdc and 0xb4. The class identity cCreatureModeStrategy is deliberately NOT promoted into the C type: the Ghidra label on the slot is App::sCreatureModeStrategy while the callee names a TYPE App::cCreatureModeStrategy, and this binary carries no RTTI (the pack's own evidence_note says so), so nothing machine-derived ties the slot to that class. void* is the weakest C type that states the observed use; it is spelled without a space so the validator's declaration regex binds the span, and the machine width (4 bytes) and void* (4 bytes on x86-32) agree.
observed_original_abi.locals: none; the body allocates no frame, saves no register and builds no record
observed_original_abi.outgoing_calls: none; the body holds no CALL, no JMP and no indirect transfer, and the committed xrefs sidecar records 0 edges out of 0x00d38840

observed_mechanics: 0x00d38840 a1 94 e2 69 01 - MOV EAX,dword ptr [0x0169e294]: opcode 0xa1 is MOV r32, moffs32, an ABSOLUTE form with no ModRM byte and no base register. The four operand bytes 94 e2 69 01 are the little-endian address 0x0169e294 itself.
0x00d38845 c3 - RET: single exit; the callee pops nothing, so stack cleanup is 0 bytes and owned by the caller.

The body is 6 bytes (0x00d38840..0x00d38845), matching the pack's body_start/body_end and body_span_bytes 6. It contains no branch, no call, no flag test, no register save and no loop: the load is unconditional, so every entry reads the slot again.
No cached, lazy, once-only or publication-checked path exists. A slot holding null comes back as a slot holding null; there is no branch with which to substitute a default.

Nothing is written. The slot is not modified by this function. Machine-level statement of that: 0xa1 is the LOAD direction of the absolute-move pair and 0xa3 is the store direction; no store appears in the body.

Raw bytes at 0x00d38840..0x00d38849, read live from the program database: a1 94 e2 69 01 c3 cc cc cc cc. The four 0xcc bytes from 0x00d38846 are INT3 padding between this entry and the next and are NOT part of the body.

Because the operand is absolute, the byte-displacement-versus-element-index hazard that a [ECX + disp] family has does not arise here: there is no index, no scale and no disp field that could be confused with a member offset.

structural_neighbours.note: The witness that makes the returned word an OBJECT POINTER rather than a scalar or a count. It is cited as context; nothing in this package's model depends on it, and this package does not reconstruct 0x00d3b9b0.

globals.bytes_in_uninitialised_image_note: Read live via read_memory. This says nothing about the running process, which is what the constructor at 0x00d3b9b0 exists to publish into the slot.
globals.modelled_as: namespace-scope SlotWord g_creature_mode_strategy_slot in the package .cpp, declared extern in the .hpp. 0x0169e294 is an address in the ORIGINAL image and is pinned as a value the test checks; the model cannot mmap that image, so the slot is stood up as a real object and read from there.
globals.not_claimed: that the slot is initialised, non-null on any particular call, immutable after construction, a singleton in any design sense, or thread-safe. 'singleton' appears only in this package's directory slug as a description of the observed one-writer shape; no synchronisation of any kind is claimed and the body has no room for a reference call. That the recorded single writer is the ONLY writer in the whole program is a fact about the pinned snapshot, not a proof about unanalysed code.

call_graph.caveat: Zero dataref rows targeting this entry means that on this pinned snapshot it is not the target of any data reference, so no vtable table reaches it. That is a recorded absence, not an exhaustive proof that no table exists. The counts are from the pinned sidecars; the live Ghidra database reports 55 xrefs to the slot and a 66-reference inbound count for this function, so the two sources agree on shape and differ on totals, which is the known DB drift.

mutation_test.isolation: every mutant is built in its own self-contained directory under /tmp/opencode/mut-00d38840-*, and BOTH the impl .cpp and the model test are compiled from THAT directory, so #include "x.hpp" resolves to the MUTATED header. The archive is deleted before every link and recreated with `ar rc`; `ar qc` would append and let a stale object silently win.

known_limits_of_this_reconstruction: The model cannot observe a write that leaves the value unchanged, so the test's sentinels do NOT cover a same-value store-through into the slot. That statement is carried by the opcode instead (0xa1 load vs 0xa3 store), pinned by static_assert in the header and perturbed as H1. This is stated in the header and in the test rather than papered over.

The test's guard words live in the test's own translation unit and are NOT guaranteed to be adjacent to the library's slot, so they catch disturbance of the test's storage and nothing more. They are not a claim about the original image's neighbouring bytes.

0x0169e294 is an address in the original image. It is pinned as a checkable constant and tied by static_assert to the encoding's moffs32, but the model reads a stood-up object rather than dereferencing that address.
unresolved_questions: What TYPE the slot's pointee is. The evidence establishes that it is an object pointer (single writer publishes `this`; callers use the result as a receiver and index through it) but does not establish its class: the Ghidra label on the slot is App::sCreatureModeStrategy while the callee names a TYPE App::cCreatureModeStrategy, and this binary has no MSVC RTTI, so nothing machine-derived ties the two together. Promoting cCreatureModeStrategy to the C type would need either RTTI, a vtable-shape match, or an SDK-proven static-member declaration.
Whether 0x00d3b9b0 is the ONLY writer across the whole program. The pinned sidecar and the live database each record one write row for the slot; neither covers unanalysed or dynamically-reached code.
Whether the slot is ever null in the running process, and therefore whether any caller has a latent null dereference. The runtime axis is GATED and unattempted, so nothing here answers it.
Whether the 39 recorded callers all use the result the same way. Four were sampled (notes above); the other 35 were not, so 'every caller treats it as a receiver' is not claimed.
